goal_checks.notes: service.go's StartRun validates cmd.Content on reqCtx, then calls RunContext(reqCtx, s.maxRunDuration) -- the exact task-010 helper (context.WithoutCancel + WithTimeout) -- before anything is handed to the supervisor. Confirmed by reading the final StartRun body and by TestServiceStartRun_ReturnsBeforeRunCompletes / TestServiceStartRun_CallerCancelAfterReturnDoesNotCancelRun passing.

TestServiceStartRun_CallerCancelAfterReturnDoesNotCancelRun cancels reqCtx immediately after StartRun returns, then releases a gated LLM call, and asserts the terminal hub event is stage.completed, not run.cancelled. Passes under -race.

grep '^\s*go\s+(func|[a-zA-Z_])' over internal/pipeline/*.go finds exactly two hits, both in hub_test.go's pre-existing TestHub_ConcurrentPublishSubscribe (task 010 test harness, not production code). orchestrator.go and service.go contain zero bare `go` statements; the only goroutine start is s.supervisor.Go(...) in StartRun.

TestServiceStartRun_PanicRecovered uses a fakeLLM that panics in Complete(); Orchestrator.Run's deferred recover marks the run Failed and publishes run.failed with message 'internal error'. The test process itself does not crash (if the recover were missing or broken, the whole test binary would abort rather than reach any assertion) -- passes under -race, and Supervisor's own recover (supervisor_test.go TestSupervisorGo_RecoversPanic) is a second, independently-tested layer.

TestServiceStartRun_Success and TestServiceStartRun_LLMError assert the exact event sequences (run.started -> stage.completed{analytic}; run.started -> run.failed) via waitForTerminal. This is the SCOPED version of g5 (see task.json's description and analyze.json open_questions) -- stage.completed only fires for analytic, and run.completed is never published, because no other stage has a real handler yet. Cross-checked against 03-backend-folder-architecture.md §9: the remaining 5 stages are explicitly step 8, three steps after this one.

TestServiceStartRun_LateSubscriberReplay waits for the run to fully finish (via a first, temporary subscription), then opens a fresh Subscribe(id, 0) and confirms the replay slice alone (no live-channel wait) contains run.started ... stage.completed{analytic}. Exercises the existing task-010 Hub ring buffer, now for the first time via real orchestrator-published events instead of hub_test.go's raw string payloads.

TestServiceStartRun_MaxConcurrentRunsQueuesOverLimit constructs a Service with maxConcurrentRuns=1, starts run 1 (gated, holds the only semaphore slot), starts run 2, and asserts run2's RunState.Status is still Pending (CurrentStage never advanced, no goroutine touched it) while run 1 is still in flight. Confirms admission-control gating happens before Supervisor.Go, not inside the goroutine.

go test -race -v ./internal/pipeline/... ./internal/shared/concurrency/... : 27 tests, 0 failures, 0 race warnings. Also ran go test -race ./... (whole module, all packages clean) and go test -race -count=8 on the same two packages specifically to rule out flakiness in the new hub-subscription synchronization -- 8/8 clean.

Matches task.json's own blocked status and blocked_reason: the Supervisor.Shutdown mechanism is fully implemented and covered by 3 dedicated -race tests (cancels-tracked-contexts, deadline-exceeded, concurrent Go+Shutdown), which is what this goal's acceptance criterion actually tests. The explicitly-deferred part (wiring Shutdown into cmd/gateway/main.go's real SIGTERM handler) is called out as blocked in task.json with a concrete, non-silent reason rather than marked done against reality.
